title: Best Time to Visit Far West Nepal, and the Flight Problem
meta_description: Best time to visit Far West Nepal month by month: Terai parks, Rara, Jumla, Khaptad, Humla and Limi, plus why monsoon and winter fog ground mountain flights.
summary: October and November are the best months for almost all of Far West Nepal, with March to May next. Bardia and Shuklaphanta are best for tigers from February to May; Humla and Limi from June to October, in the rain shadow. The catch is flying: monsoon cloud and winter fog ground small planes.

sections.heading: One region, three climates
paras: Far West Nepal spans almost every climate the country has. The Terai, at 100 to 200 m around Bardia, Dhangadhi and Shuklaphanta, is subtropical: hot from April to June, wet from mid-June to September, and cool, foggy and dry in winter. The middle hills and high valleys of Karnali and Sudurpashchim, including Jumla at about 2,540 m, Rara at 2,990 m and Khaptad at about 3,000 m, have warm summers with monsoon rain and cold, sometimes snowy winters.

Upper Humla and the Limi valley, north of the main Himalayan range, are different again. They lie in the rain shadow, so the monsoon arrives weakened, and summer is the best time to walk there, while winter brings deep cold and snow on the passes. The right month therefore depends on what you want to do. The table below summarises it; the sections that follow explain why.

sections.heading: Spring: tigers, flowers and heat
paras: From February to May the Terai parks are at their best for wildlife. In winter, local villagers are allowed into the parks for a short period to cut thatch grass, which opens up the phanta grasslands. As temperatures rise, water becomes scarce and animals gather along the rivers, which is when guides in Bardia sit on riverbanks for tigers. The cost is heat: afternoons in May can pass 40 °C, so activities shift to early mornings and evenings.

In the hills, spring brings rhododendron flowering in red, pink and white from March to May, warmer days at Rara and Khaptad and generally good flying weather. Haze from dust and forest fires can soften mountain views by late April and May. For Rara and Khaptad, April and May are the second-best season after autumn.

sections.heading: Monsoon and the flight problem
paras: From mid-June to September the monsoon reaches western Nepal. It is usually lighter here than in the east, but still enough to flood the Terai rivers, close the national parks to most activities, trigger landslides on hill roads and fill forests with leeches. Most Terai lodges close or operate a skeleton service.

The bigger issue for travellers is flying. Jumla, Talcha and Simikot are reached by small aircraft from Nepalgunj, landing on short mountain strips that need clear visibility. In the monsoon, cloud often sits on the ridges for days, and flights are cancelled or delayed, sometimes several days in a row. Supplies to remote districts also depend on these flights, so seats can be scarce when flights resume. This is the monsoon flight problem: you may be able to walk happily in Humla's rain shadow, but you may not be able to get there, or get out, on schedule.

That does not mean monsoon travel is impossible. Limi and upper Humla treks run successfully in July and August, and Khaptad's meadows are at their flowering peak then. But you must plan with generous buffers and accept that your dates may move.

sections.heading: Autumn: the best of everything
paras: October and November are the best months for nearly every part of the far west. The monsoon clears, skies are sharp and blue, roads dry out, and flights become far more reliable. In the Terai the parks reopen, green and cool, and wildlife viewing is good though not as concentrated as in spring. In Jumla the red rice and apples are harvested, and in the high valleys of Limi barley is brought in before winter.

Autumn is also festival season: Dashain and Tihar bring families together, and many Nepali visitors travel to Rara and Khaptad during the holidays. Book flights and lodges early, and be aware that government offices close for several days around Dashain, which can affect permit processing.
If you can travel only once, make it the second half of October: the rains are gone, the festival crowds have thinned after Dashain, and the high country is still warm enough for comfortable camping.

sections.heading: Winter: fog below, snow above
paras: From December to February the Terai enjoys dry, mild afternoons, but mornings bring thick fog, especially in late December and January. Fog can delay flights into Nepalgunj and Dhangadhi for hours. Safaris still run, with cold dawn drives and fewer animals at the rivers. In the hills, nights at Jumla and Rara fall well below freezing, snow can block trails and the Rara lodges see very few visitors. The passes of Humla and Limi are closed.

Winter suits travellers who want quiet Terai parks, Tharu villages during Maghi in mid-January, or heritage trips to warmer sites such as Dullu and Surkhet. It is not a season for trekking in the far western hills.

Whatever the season, pack for a range of temperatures. A trip that starts in Bardia at 35 °C can end a week later at Rara with frost on the tent. Light, breathable clothes for the plain, a warm down jacket for the hills, a rain shell from June to September and a good sun hat cover nearly every combination. Sunscreen matters at altitude even when the air feels cold.
list: Keep at least one spare day after any mountain flight out of Jumla, Talcha or Simikot.
Book the earliest morning flights; they are the most likely to operate.
Do not book international departures within two days of a Karnali trek.
Carry enough cash for extra nights; there are few ATMs in the hills.
Buy travel insurance that covers delays and helicopter evacuation.

sections.heading: Choosing by destination
paras: Bardia and Shuklaphanta: come between October and May. For the best chance of a tiger, choose March to May and accept the heat; for comfort and green landscapes, choose October and November. Shuklaphanta's swamp deer gather on the open grassland in the largest herds from February to April, when fresh grass grows after the winter cutting and burning.

Rara Lake and Jumla: October and November first, April and May second. In autumn the skies are clearest, the Talcha and Jumla flights most reliable, and Jumla's red rice and apples are being harvested. In spring the forests flower and nights are less cold, but haze can hide distant peaks by May. Avoid December to February unless you are prepared for deep cold.

Khaptad and Ramaroshan: April and May for rhododendron and settled weather, October and November for clear views. The monsoon months bring the famous Khaptad flowers but also rain, leeches and difficult roads through Doti and Achham. The Ganga Dashahara fair at Khaptad, usually in late May or June, is worth planning around if you enjoy crowds and music.

Humla and Limi: June to October. Choose September and early October for harvest, clearer skies and better flights; choose July and August only if you are flexible about dates. Dullu, Surkhet and the Khasa heritage sites are lower and warmer, and can be visited from October to April, including winter.

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Far West Nepal?
faqs.a: October is the single best month for most of the region: clear skies, dry roads, reliable flights and harvest season in Jumla. November is nearly as good, slightly colder. For tigers in Bardia, March to May is better. For Humla and Limi, June to October works best because of the rain shadow.

faqs.q: Can I visit Bardia during the monsoon?
faqs.a: Most of Bardia National Park closes to jungle activities from mid-June to September, when rivers flood and tracks become impassable, and many lodges close or reduce services. You may be able to visit villages and the park headquarters, but wildlife viewing is very limited. Plan Bardia between October and May.

faqs.q: Why are flights to Jumla and Simikot often cancelled?
faqs.a: Small aircraft land on short mountain airstrips that require clear visibility and calm wind. In the monsoon, low cloud often covers the ridges, and in winter, fog on the plain can delay departures from Nepalgunj. Flights operate mainly in the morning. Delays of one or more days are common, so buffer days are essential.

faqs.q: Is winter a good time for Rara Lake?
faqs.a: Only for hardy travellers. From December to February nights at Rara fall well below freezing, snow can cover trails and the area around the lake, lodges are cold and many services close. Days can be bright and clear. Most visitors prefer October–November or April–May.

faqs.q: When do rhododendrons bloom in the Far West?
faqs.a: From March to May, depending on altitude. Lower forests in Doti and Dailekh bloom first, in March; higher forests at Khaptad, Ramaroshan and on the Rara trek peak in April and early May. The red flowers of the national flower cover whole hillsides in a good year.

faqs.q: Is it too hot to visit the Terai in May?
faqs.a: May is very hot, with afternoon temperatures often near or above 40 °C, but it is also one of the best months for tiger sightings, because animals stay close to water. Safaris run at dawn and late afternoon, and you rest in the middle of the day. Choose a lodge with fans or air conditioning.

faqs.q: Can I trek in Humla in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Yes. Upper Humla and Limi lie in the rain shadow of the main Himalaya, so they receive far less rain than the south, and the passes are snow-free from June to early October. The problem is flights between Nepalgunj and Simikot, which are less reliable. Allow two or three spare days.

faqs.q: What is the weather like in Jumla?
faqs.a: Jumla, at about 2,540 m, has warm days and cool nights from April to October, with monsoon rain from late June to September. Winters are cold, with frost most nights and occasional snow in the valley. October and November give the clearest, driest weather and the harvest of red rice and apples.

faqs.q: When is the Khaptad flower season?
faqs.a: Khaptad's meadows flower most heavily during the monsoon, from about June to August, when the patans are covered in wildflowers. It is beautiful but wet, with cloud, rain and leeches on the approach. April–May and October–November give clearer skies with fewer flowers, and are better for most trekkers.
